references.text: Fire came out from the Lord's presence and consumed the burnt offering and the fat portions on the altar, a parallel to the fire that rises from the rock and consumes the meat and the unleavened cakes.
The Lord's fire fell down and consumed the burnt offering on Carmel, similar divine confirmation through fire as in Gideon's case.
The Lord answered with fire from heaven on the burnt offering altar, the same pattern of divine fire as a sign of acceptance.
Manoah offered to the Lord, and the angel of the Lord rose up in the altar flame and disappeared, very similar to the event with Gideon where the angel disappears after the fire.
Abraham met three men/angels, and one of them was identified as the Lord, a similar theophany to Gideon's meeting with the angel of the Lord.
The angel of the Lord revealed himself to Moses in a flame, the same divine messenger who appeared to Gideon.
